reason: Adding dust to the disk seems like a useful start toward making pebbles.
expectation: The falling dust will enter the young star's disk, possibly enabling grains to gather.

alternatives.reason: The inward-moving icy grains may also supply the warm disk, but I would first follow the incoming dust.

effect: The dust has settled into the disk's crowded middle plane, where it can meet other grains.
reaction: The role of gas drag in concentrating the dust is interesting.
reason: Slowly meeting grains seem likely to stick to the settled dust and help build pebbles.
expectation: The grains may form larger aggregates, though they might not become pebbles immediately.

alternatives.reason: The inward-moving icy grains could also supply the warm disk, but I want to follow the settled dust first.

effect: Gentle collisions made fragile clumps rather than pebbles; a harder collision may reveal their broken pieces.
reaction: The contrast between gentle growth and easy breakage is interesting.
reason: Fast crossing grains could break the fluffy clumps, advancing the goal of following their fragments.
expectation: The collision will likely break the clumps into smaller pieces, though their exact form is unclear.

alternatives.reason: The icy grains may supply the warm disk, but I want to follow the fragile clumps first.

effect: The fast collision broke the clumps into smaller grains, which can now interact with settled dust.
reaction: The reversal of their earlier growth is clear and satisfying.
reason: Combining the shattered grains with settled dust follows the fragments toward the chapter goal.
expectation: The fragments may join other dust and begin gathering again, though the result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The icy grains could help supply the warm disk, but I want to follow the shattered pieces first.

effect: The shattered grains rebuilt into clumps, completing the goal of following the fragments.
reaction: It's satisfying to see the broken material rejoin a gathering.
reason: This is the only available combination and may advance the remaining warm-disk goal.
expectation: The icy grains will enter the warm disk, where their ice may evaporate; I'm unsure how that supplies pebbles.

effect: The warm disk evaporated the ice, leaving rocky grains that can now meet slowly moving grains.
reaction: The distinction between evaporating and vanishing is useful.
reason: This is the only available combination and may build the remaining pebble supply.
expectation: The rocky grains may stick together and grow into pebbles or larger clumps.

effect: Gentle encounters built the dry grains into rocky pebbles, which can now combine with the rebuilt clumps.
reaction: The distinction between pebbles and a finished planet is useful.
reason: This is the only available combination and may complete the warm-disk pebble goal.
expectation: The pebbles and rebuilt clumps may form a larger gathering or provide the disk with its pebble supply; the exact result is unclear.

effect: The pebbles swept up some smaller material, completing the warm-disk supply and the chapter.
reaction: It's satisfying that the rebuilt fragments remain part of the mixed supply rather than all becoming pebbles.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following fragile clumps through breakage and rebuilding was most worthwhile: it made growth and fragmentation feel like connected processes.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final pebble-supply combination felt less engaging because it was the only available action and its exact purpose was not yet clear.

surprise.text: I was interested that ice evaporated in the warm disk while the rocky grains remained, rather than the material simply disappearing.

arbitrary.text: Combining pebbles with rebuilt clumps initially felt a little unclear, though the result explained that pebbles sweep up smaller material.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue: the cycle of breakage and regrowth made me curious about what happens to the pebble supply next.
